REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JUNE 14, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT HELD ON JUNE 14,
2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by City Council Member Jim Edwards.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Recreation Services Teen Volunteer Cameron
  Campbell.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

4.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Martin Grossman requested additional public comment opportunities prior to the
  adoption of the Fiscal Year 2018-2019 budget and expressed concern regarding
  budget deficits and succession planning.

  Gail Grossman expressed concern regarding the proposed Fiscal Year 2018-2019
  budget, including the addition of Councilmember benefits, adoption of the Capital
  Improvement Program and various staff positions.

  Anantha Ramachandran requested an income flow statement placed in front of the
  final budget document and expressed concerns regarding budget deficits and the
  proposed Capital Improvement Program.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern regarding the length of presentations, recognition of
  various community groups, permit fee costs, the cost of running the Cerritos Center
  for the Performing Arts, and continued support for the Neighborhood Watch
  Program.

  Murali Vasudevan thanked the Mayor for acknowledging Asian-American Pacific
  Islander Heritage Month, expressed concern for the length of presentations and
  expressed concern regarding the public review period for the proposed Fiscal Year
  2018-2019 budget.

  Katherine George Chu expressed concern regarding the proximity of alcohol
  establishments and a billboard advertising alcoholic beverages at Pioneer Boulevard
  and 167th Street, near Niemes Elementary School.

  C.W. Van der Linden thanked the City Council and staff for recent trimming of pine
  trees and expressed support for the City’s current tree trimming vendor.

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt AN URGENCY
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ESTABLISHING A MORATORIUM ON NEW OR
  EXPANDED SELF-STORAGE FACILITIES AND PROHIBITING THE ISSUANCE OF
  BUILDING PERMITS, USE PERMITS, AND OTHER LAND USE ENTITLEMENTS RELATED
  THERETO (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was given.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Gene Sais spoke regarding his meeting with Council on a proposed property, the status
  of his business plan, and submitted documents for the record.

  Mayor Pulido noted for the record that he did meet with interested parties in the
  development of the subject property and that they were advised of the pending
  moratorium.

  John Bowen, property owner, commented regarding development of the site and
  expressed his opposition to the moratorium.

  Anantha Ramachandran expressed concern regarding the proposed moratorium when
  there are more pressing concerns in the City.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the
  public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, seconded by Hu, to waive full reading of and
  adopt ORDINANCE No. 1020, AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS ESTABLISHING A MORATORIUM ON NEW OR EXPANDED SELF-
  STORAGE FACILITIES AND PROHIBITING THE ISSUANCE OF BUILDING
  PERMITS, USE PERMITS, AND OTHER LAND USE ENTITLEMENTS RELATED
  THERETO (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 14, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational report to the Cerritos City Council
  regarding the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority's proposed
  West Santa Ana Branch (WSAB) transit corridor light rail project, with emphasis on
  the proposed southern alignment traversing through the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager and Torrey
  Contreras, Director of Community Development. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  Manjeet Ranu, Metro Senior Executive Officer, and Melani Smith, Metro Senior
  Director Transit Oriented Communities, presented the Metro proposed corridor project
  overview. A PowerPoint presentation was given.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Anantha Ramachandran thanked the Metro for their work and presentation, spoke
  regarding Measure M, and expressed support for the Metro project.

  Katherine George Chu commented that the community supports Measure M and
  expressed support for the Metro project.

  C.W. Van der Linden expressed his opposition to the Metro project.

  Cheryl Davis expressed her opposition to the Metro project and believes the
  majority of Metro users will be Orange County residents.

  Roger Garrett commented on transportation with respect to public safety and Los
  Angeles County parking fees.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, seconded by Hu, to:
  1.  Authorize the City of Cerritos to continue to participate in Metro’s
  environmental analysis, TOD strategic implementation plan, and station
  location studies; and

  2.  Authorize a Metro-hosted community workshop to be hosted at a Cerritos
  community facility, to solicit additional input from the Cerritos community,
  including residential and commercial stakeholders; and,

  3.  Receive and file the report (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 14, 2018
